messages.content: I want to settle the San Diego flights now. Compare all three for the two of us, including the one checked bag we would share. I care about the actual total and how much of November 8 and 13 we would have in San Diego.

Here is the current comparison for MSP-SAN, November 8-13. Option 1 is Sun Country nonstop: 6:20 a.m. outbound, arriving 8:12 a.m.; return at 8:45 p.m., arriving MSP at 2:14 a.m. Saturday. Base fare is $758 for two, and one checked bag adds $90 round trip, for $848 total. Seat selection is not included. It gives you nearly all of both travel days, but the return gets you home very late.

Option 2 is Delta nonstop in both directions. It leaves MSP at 9:05 a.m. and reaches San Diego at 11:08 a.m. The return leaves at 1:20 p.m. and arrives at 6:53 p.m. Base fare for two is $948; one shared checked bag adds $70 round trip, making the flight total $1,018. Standard seat selection and carry-ons are included.
So that is $170 more than Sun Country after bags. What exactly do we give up in San Diego?

About three hours on arrival day and seven hours on departure day. In exchange, you avoid a pre-dawn airport trip from Minneapolis and the after-2:00 a.m. arrival home. Both options are nonstop, so the difference is mainly usable destination time versus easier travel hours.
Run the connecting option too. I remember the fare looked closer to the cheap one.

Option 3 is Alaska Airlines at $812 for two before baggage. The outbound leaves MSP at 8:15 a.m., connects in Seattle for 1 hour 22 minutes, and arrives in San Diego at 2:47 p.m. The return is nonstop at 3:10 p.m., arriving MSP at 8:42 p.m. One shared checked bag is $35 each way, so the total is $882. That is only $34 above Sun Country, but you would arrive more than six and a half hours later and take on connection risk.
Please put each one against the single-hotel plan. Use the latest hotel total, not the split stay.

The five-night single-property hotel total is still $2,041 including taxes and mandatory fees. Combined airfare and lodging would be $2,889 with Sun Country, $3,059 with Delta, or $2,923 with Alaska. All three remain below the $3,600 ceiling: the respective cushions are $711, $541, and $677. Those figures include the shared checked bag but exclude optional seat fees on Sun Country.
Alaska does not seem worth saving $136 versus Delta if it burns most of Sunday afternoon. Is there any hidden basic-economy restriction on Delta?

The quoted Delta fare is Main Cabin, not Basic Economy. Seats can be selected before check-in, changes are permitted subject to any fare difference, and the ticket is nonrefundable to the original payment method. The checked-bag charge is already included in the $1,018 comparison total.

Then choose Delta. The $170 premium over Sun Country is reasonable for normal travel hours, and we still have more than $500 left under the cap. Keep the single hotel plan and leave the split stay aside.

Selected plan: Delta Main Cabin nonstop round trip for two, November 8-13, at $1,018 including one shared checked bag. Outbound departs MSP at 9:05 a.m. and arrives SAN at 11:08 a.m.; return departs SAN at 1:20 p.m. and arrives MSP at 6:53 p.m. With the five-night single-property hotel at $2,041, the airfare-and-lodging total is $3,059, leaving $541 under the $3,600 ceiling. Alaska and Sun Country are declined, and the split stay is set aside. The Delta flights and hotel still need a final live-price and terms check before purchase; nothing has been booked.
